judgment.rationale: Both Skills sit in the same resolved coordinate (Grade R, rank 0) and the same Term 4 / Emergent Reading / Phonological-Phonemic Awareness cell on page 55, so direction cannot rest on grade or term order and needs substantive statement evidence. The second SFI works at the coarsest grain of phonological awareness: segmenting an oral sentence into individual words, clapping each word and deliberately starting with one-syllable words ('It is time for lunch'). The first SFI operates at a finer grain inside a single word: relating sounds to letters and words and understanding that a word is made of more than one sound ('duck is d-u-ck', done aurally). Its LC tags ('phonemic awareness', 'segmenting', 'sounds', 'phonics') versus the second's ('phonological awareness', 'segmenting', 'sentences', 'words') confirm this sentence-to-word versus word-to-phoneme contrast rather than generic repeated wording. Hearing and isolating discrete word units in speech supports the likelihood of success in then hearing discrete sounds within a word, so the second builds towards the first; the reverse finer-to-coarser direction is not supported. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (24 omitted items each) and both carry upstream merge/audit context, so this is an inference from the printed bullets available, not from the full cell.
